reviewer: Claude Code session (Claude Fable 5.1); post-fix verification of the 2026-09-05 baseline by the same rubric at merged main revisions; no new blind sample

rubric.meaning: Review index, not probability, effectiveness, or behavioral benchmark. 100 means no scored findings within stated coverage. Findings can remain even when a model compensates. Plugin packaging score is separate from mean skill score.
rubric.scope: 33 owned canonical skill entrypoints in 6 plugins. Third-party/system skills and legacy personal copies are inventory-only, not scored. Post-fix pass re-reviews every entity in scope against the same rubric; resolved findings are retained below with status and fix commits.

findings.title: GitHits frontmatter fails the authoritative validator
findings.detail: The unquoted description contains colon-space sequences. Both PyYAML and claude plugin validate reject it. Claude validator reports metadata will be dropped at runtime. Catalog CI only regex-checks field presence, so it misses this defect.
findings.recommendation: Use a YAML block scalar and run a real YAML parser and host validator in CI.
findings.verification: PyYAML parses the frontmatter; claude plugin validate passes code-tools; validate_plugins.py and CI regression test enforce real YAML parsing.

findings.title: Release dry-run can discard pre-existing edits
findings.detail: The dry-run edits real files and then runs git checkout -- <files>. A scratch Git reproduction lost an existing userNote field. The dirty-tree warning does not preserve the original bytes.
findings.recommendation: Generate the proposed diff in a temporary copy, or restore an exact pre-run snapshot without discarding user changes.
findings.verification: Instruction rewritten to work on temporary copies and forbid git restore/checkout/reset as cleanup. Not re-executed by an agent in this pass.

findings.title: Rust scaffold verification does not compile tests
findings.detail: A fixture with a type error inside an ignored cfg(test) test passes cargo check (0) and fails cargo test --no-run (101). The skill promises scaffold compilation but selects the weaker command.
findings.recommendation: Use cargo test --no-run or cargo check --tests with the owning crate and feature configuration.
findings.verification: Fixture re-run: cargo check exit 0, cargo test --no-run exit 101 on the same type error; the skill now mandates the latter (reproductions.json).

findings.title: Accessibility inventory misses Astro and templ
findings.detail: The inventory omits .astro and .templ yet instructs the agent to stop on zero. A fixture containing index.astro returns 0 files and the stop instruction. This is a detection gap in stacks maintained by this marketplace.
findings.recommendation: Include supported template extensions and treat zero probe matches as a hypothesis until the target surface is checked.
findings.verification: Fixture with index.astro and view.templ returns "2 files" in bash and zsh; stop instruction replaced (reproductions.json, regression test).

findings.title: Git guard does not cover common executable forms
findings.detail: Payload-only tests deny git commit --no-verify but silently allow /usr/bin/git commit --no-verify and env git commit --no-verify. No commit commands were executed. This is incomplete convenience-hook coverage, not proof that repository CI can be bypassed.
findings.recommendation: Narrow the documented guarantee; normalize supported invocation forms and retain authoritative checks outside the agent hook.
findings.verification: /usr/bin/git, env, env -i, command, and git -C forms now deny; plain git push -n and echo remain allowed (reproductions.json, regression test). Header narrows the guarantee.

findings.title: Test-scaffold discovery promises more than the body permits
findings.detail: JS, Go and Rust descriptions trigger on write tests/add coverage, while bodies mandate todo/skip/ignore stubs and forbid assertions. One blind Codex sample correctly prioritized an explicit request for assertions: 4/4 artifact criteria met. This finding is the contradictory contract, not a demonstrated failure of that sample.
findings.recommendation: Limit discovery to explicit scaffolding, or make complete tests the default when requested and stubs an explicit mode.
findings.verification: Three descriptions limit discovery to explicit scaffolding; bodies redirect working-test requests to executable assertions. Static review; no discovery test run.

findings.title: Generic scaffold fallback still mandates starter styling
findings.detail: Astro component-scaffold and Go templ-component-scaffold allow alternate layouts but still prescribe Tailwind and starter tokens. This contradicts plugin claims of fallback support for other projects. Verified instruction mismatch; no generated UI was evaluated.
findings.recommendation: Read the target styling system and make starter classes conditional on the starter being present.
findings.verification: Both scaffolds read the target styling system first and make starter classes conditional. Static review; no generated UI evaluated.

findings.title: Build freshness rule omits uncommitted edits
findings.detail: Astro perf-budget-check uses the last committed src timestamp versus dist mtime. An uncommitted source edit leaves the git log timestamp unchanged, so this method cannot establish working-tree artifact freshness. Static algorithm review; no production build or perf gate run.
findings.recommendation: Use the repository build/cache fingerprint or rebuild before reporting working-tree budgets.
findings.verification: Freshness rule requires a rebuild or repository fingerprint; timestamps excluded; unverifiable builds report as not run. Static review.

findings.title: Skill audit treats allowed-tools as a restrictive boundary
findings.detail: The audit says underscoping allowed-tools breaks runtime. Current Claude documentation describes it as an approval grant; separate restrictions govern tool removal. The body also assumes universal undertriggering without a model-specific evaluation.
findings.recommendation: Audit approval grants separately from restrictions and test triggering per host/model rather than using a permanent assumption.
findings.verification: skill-audit and MAINTAINING.md treat allowed-tools as an approval grant and require per-host discovery tests. Static review.

findings.title: Pezza mark instructions have an unresolved exception
findings.detail: The hard rule says never filled/outlined, while the file map and production guidance explicitly provide official filled outlines for static placement. The intended distinction between altering artwork and using official assets should be explicit. No visual defect is claimed.
findings.recommendation: State that official filled artwork is permitted and that the no-fill rule concerns modifying the stroke master.
findings.verification: Rule 3 distinguishes altering the stroke master from placing official filled artwork. Static review.

findings.title: Ideation requires a second user override
findings.detail: The escape hatch requires pushing back once when the user says just move on, respecting only a second pushback. This adds friction for already explicit scope choices. Instruction review only, not a behavioral failure.
findings.recommendation: Respect the first explicit override while recording unresolved assumptions.
findings.verification: Escape hatch respects the first explicit override and records open assumptions. Static review; committed on branch fix/ideation-first-override.
